summary: Colville Reservation lookout: a 1934 L-4 ground cab stands beside the staffed 1960s steel tower; the cab is in very poor shape and a reservation use pass is required.

facts.design: 1934 L-4 ground cab, about a quarter mile northeast of a 53-foot all-steel live-in tower built in the 1960s
facts.status_note: The 1934 L-4 cab is still on site in very poor condition; the steel tower is the staffed lookout

access.note: Colville Reservation land. Visitors need a reservation use pass. SummitPost warns that access for non-tribal members can change at any time. The steel tower is locked.

visit.trail_note: Road conditions on the Colville can vary dramatically year to year; TrailChick advises a high-clearance 4x4. The cab site is just northeast of the summit and takes some hunting to find.

facts.agency: Confederated Tribes of the Colville Reservation (register: Colville Indian Reservation)

events.note: L-4 ground cab, about a quarter mile northeast of the current steel lookout. Register and TrailChick date it 1934.
Indian department working on the mountain in June 1934: a camp, lumber hauled up, poles being cut and a trail being built.
Three-legged 60-foot wooden tower with 7x7 cab, built by the CCC for a reported $1,046 with the cab. Fire Lookout and SummitPost date the tower to 1938.
Teachers hired as summer fire lookouts in the Colville National Forest; a 1943 newspaper names one on Whitmore Mountain.
Inspection report calls the wooden tower unsafe and proposes a 50-foot steel tower with quarters on top. The steel tower that followed was built in the 1960s.
Letter suggests moving the new tower about a quarter mile southwest, onto privately owned land.
Lightning started the Whitmore fire on August 3, 2021. Crews dug a hand line around the historic L-4 cab and wrapped it; both lookouts survived.

corrections.proposed: 1934 built (L-4 ground cab, not the current structure)
corrections.why: The 1934 L-4 cab is the ground cab. The current lookout is the 1960s steel tower, so 'Current structure' is wrong.
Duplicate of us-wa-whitmore-mountain (same register entry, US 1565, WA 92), which is verified. This record's point is about 250 m away. For editor decision.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Register and TrailChick give 1934 for the L-4 cab and 1935 for the tower. Fire Lookout and SummitPost give 1938. The 1960 inspection report gives 1935 for the structures. We follow the register's dates and say the others disagree. TrailChick's header 'Current Structure Built: 1934' conflicts with its own text; we read it as the cab date.
Steel tower height: 53 feet in the register, TrailChick, Fire Lookout and Okanogan Country; 67 feet in SummitPost. The story reports both.

notes_for_editor: This record duplicates us-wa-whitmore-mountain (verified, with register number US 1565, WA 92); the story follows this record's subject, the 1934 L-4 cab. Build dates conflict (1934/1935 against 1938) and the story says so. Steel tower height conflicts (53 against 67 feet). The staffing 'every summer' claim comes from the register and two guides. The $80 annual pass is from a tribal PDF whose URL timestamp dates it to April 2024; recheck the price before publishing. Access is reservation land: visitors need a use pass, and SummitPost warns that access for non-tribal members can change. The story does not encourage climbing.
